title: Limit Theorems
intro: What happens to averages and sums of many random variables. The law of large numbers says averages settle on the mean; the central limit theorem says how they fluctuate around it. Monte Carlo methods turn both into a way of computing.

items: Modes of Convergence (#/probability/limit-theorems/modes-of-convergence): almost surely, in probability, in mean square and in distribution, and how they relate.
The Law of Large Numbers (#/probability/limit-theorems/law-of-large-numbers): weak and strong forms, and what goes wrong without a mean.
The Central Limit Theorem (#/probability/limit-theorems/central-limit-theorem): why sums look normal, how fast, and when they do not.
Monte Carlo Methods (#/probability/limit-theorems/monte-carlo): computing integrals and probabilities by simulation, and reducing the error.
R. Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th edition, Cambridge University Press (2019), chapters 2 and 3
G. R. Grimmett and D. R. Stirzaker, Probability and Random Processes, 4th edition, Oxford University Press (2020), chapter 7
